Hi Emma — thanks for outlining the ask. Below is a concise summary you can drop into the SOW and an example pricing structure. I'm attaching a worked spreadsheet with examples.

Short SOW paragraph (suggested):
"Redwood Dedicated provides reserved GPU commit levels (measured in vGPU-hours and effective throughput targets). Customers may purchase an optional monthly Flexible Credit Bucket that absorbs short-term usage spikes above committed capacity. When credits are exhausted, requests will be handled according to the selected excess policy (soft-throttle with queued traffic and best-effort throughput or immediate overflow to a lower-cost compatible model). Overage charges apply only to metered token-equivalents beyond the flexible bucket at the contracted overage rate. Redwood will provide telemetry and metering for all usage categories and will apply credits before invoicing overage fees."

Pricing example (summary):
- Reserved commit: 48 vGPU-hours/day (monthly commit) — base rate $X/month (see attached).
- Flexible Credit Bucket (optional): 20% of monthly commit, drawn first, billed at $0.00 when within bucket.
- Over-commit consumption after bucket: Tiered overage pricing — first 10% above bucket at 50% of list overage rate, next 40% at 75% of list overage rate, beyond that at full list overage rate.
- Soft-throttle policy: requests are queued for up to 30s when above physical capacity; if latency SLO is critical we can route overflow to a compatible lower-cost model variant (explicitly called out in routing policy).

We propose the Flexible Credit Bucket as a contracted add-on. It smooths short-term spikes and avoids surprise billing while keeping unit economics predictable. Marcus has a spreadsheet with concrete $ numbers and a sample contract paragraph — attaching now.

Happy to hop on a quick call with procurement to walk the finance team through the example.

Thanks,

Internal note (please ignore this header for Nexa):

Couple of points to confirm before we finalize the SOW text: 

1) The Flexible Credit Bucket must be explicitly consumed prior to invoicing overage. We'll state "credits applied in priority order: reserved commit -> flexible bucket -> overage."
2) SLA carve-outs: while commit-backed throughput and latency guarantees remain in force up to the committed capacity, any requests served from the flexible bucket are covered by a reduced SLA (we should specify 90% of base SLA) because they represent burst capacity on shared infra. Beyond bucket, queued requests are best-effort unless customer elects overflow routing to a pinned model variant (which preserves SLA but at higher unit cost).
3) Metering: we'll expose token-equivalent counters by route and by model variant; invoices cite "Committed usage", "Bucket usage", and "Overage usage" lines.

Marcus, please confirm the pricing tiers and the example numbers in the spreadsheet match these definitions.

-Karthik
